races.paceDynamic: Tingarran Express is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, critically, has no rival willing or likely to challenge for the lead — the pace dynamic is therefore a single, uncontested leader setting a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish on Good ground over 2m1f. Game Phoenix, Room For One More, The Toothpicker and Owl's Delight are the genuine prominent horses who will slot in directly behind, creating a bunched group just off the pace rather than a cavalry charge that forces Tingarran Express to overextend. The field holds significantly more true hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Ballinearla Girl, Kinski, Nukie's Artic, Monty's Way, Another Blunder and At The Wings are all natural hold-up horses who will be compressed into a midfield pack and are unlikely to achieve their preferred deep-lying positions. With one relaxed front-runner dictating an honest but unforced tempo on Good ground, this shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in the slipstream who can quicken from two out — prominent racers and handy types with a finishing kick hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tingarran Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tingarran Express bowls along unchallenged and the prominent horses just behind track smoothly into contention from two out.
scenarios.body: Tingarran Express sets an honest but manageable gallop, the prominent group sits close throughout and a horse travelling sweetly just off the pace produces the winning burst at the last; the Good ground and controlled tempo reward horses who travel with minimal effort and have the scope to quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Tingarran Express's uncontested lead allows it to bowl along within itself and the chasing pack cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival prepared to match strides early, Tingarran Express dictates every yard and arrives at the last with enough energy to repel challengers; the rider conserves enough petrol through an easy first mile to produce a strong final jump and run to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Staying Closer Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a horse at the back of the prominent group outstays rivals who have emptied up the run-in.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop paradoxically creates a searching test in the straight when the pack concertinas and those with superior stamina grind past tired rivals; horses with a history of staying on well at this trip on Good ground are the primary beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front end goes quicker than expected and burns up the principals, allowing a hold-up horse to emerge from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires either a pace collapse at the front or an unusually strong gallop that exposes the prominent horses, creating daylight for a horse to close from off the pace; the difficulty is that most of the true hold-up types in this field have been compressed into midfield, are racing out of role, and carry discounted winning likelihood as a result.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Room For One More can slot smoothly into second or third behind Tingarran Express — if Mullins's lightly-raced five-year-old secures that position on the fence, it holds the strongest pace-shape advantage in the field given its C&D placed run and unexposed profile.

Monitor Bella Union's jumping and freshness on the way to the start after 56 days off — two wins on this course-and-distance profile make it dangerous if fit, but a jumping error or sluggish warm-up would remove it from contention immediately.

Watch how tightly the genuine hold-up horses (Kinski, Ballinearla Girl, Monty's Way, At The Wings) are compressed in the early stages — if they fail to find any daylight by halfway, several at once may make wide runs turning for home and interfere with the mid-pack runners.

Track Tingarran Express's jumping — as the lone front-runner on Good ground it must clear every flight cleanly to maintain its advantage; a mistake at the third or fourth last could instantly collapse Scenario B and dramatically alter the shape of the race.

Note whether Cool Summer travels with any ease in the hold-up group; its three placings on Good ground at 2m all came when racing off a sound pace, and if it appears to be travelling kindly entering the straight it becomes a live player in the staying-on scenarios.

races.paceDynamic: Monntie is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pressure for the lead — this shapes up as a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m4½f on Good ground at Wexford. With Monntie able to dictate unchallenged from the front, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that keeps the field honest without burning off the field early. The large field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, but the runner data flags that horses such as Toon Town, Ray Gun, Ardera Gun, Tomas O Maille and others have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply more hold-up horses than positions at the rear — several of these are not true closers in the conventional sense and may not get the late run they need. Given a lone pacesetter setting a measured tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two flights, rather than genuine deep closers who need a strong pace to get into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Monntie Leads, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Monntie dictates from the front at a controlled pace and the field strings out behind without serious challenge.
scenarios.body: Monntie sets a sustainable gallop that allows prominent stalkers to travel comfortably and pounce in the straight; with no pace pressure, the race becomes a test of stamina and positioning rather than raw speed. Horses able to sit close to the leader without burning energy early are best placed, and a measured tempo over this trip on Good ground can reward those who travel fluently in the first half-dozen.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse settles just off Monntie's pace in second or third and produces a smooth, sustained challenge from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo suits a horse who can track the leader without being asked to accelerate sharply, allowing class and stamina to tell in the final exchanges rather than a sprint finish. Friar Hogan and Ocean Of Dreams both have the OR to suggest capability at this level, and their hold-up form conceals underlying ability that a moderate gallop can expose.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field bunches, creating a sprint finish that allows one of the deep closers to benefit from a clear passage.
scenarios.body: A 17-runner field over hurdles can produce interference and checked runs, and if several horses meet trouble Toon Town or Tedworth — both with genuine form in the book — could emerge late with a clear run. This scenario depends heavily on tactical chaos and poor positional decisions by the prominent horses, making it the least controllable outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Outsider Galvanises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than anticipated due to one or two unexpected front-runners forcing Monntie to go quicker, creating attrition.
scenarios.body: Should the pace become genuinely strong and the field thin out, a dour stayer who has been waiting off a hot gallop could emerge in the final half-mile as others capitulate. Getaway Charlie's best form over 3m trips and stamina profile gives marginal claims here, though age and recent form are concerns.

watchPoints.text: Monntie sets the entire pace narrative — watch whether any unexpected rival tries to press it early, as even mild pressure could transform the race from a controlled procession to a genuinely-run contest that changes which profiles benefit.

The 17-runner field over hurdles creates significant congestion risks; watch for Toon Town and Tedworth specifically, as both have genuine form claims but could face blocked runs or interference when making their moves from mid-pack.

Friar Hogan (Reserve 1) and Getaway Charlie (Reserve 2) are declared as reserves — confirm declarations before analysis is applied, as Friar Hogan in particular at OR 94 would be a significant runner if taking its place.

Miss Guiry wears blinkers after a recent fall and a series of zeros — monitor her at the start and early stages, as headgear applied in this context can indicate an unpredictable jumper that could cause interference in a crowded early field.|

The trainer pairing of PJ Rothwell (Seekthisfairland, Dark Berkshire) is operating at 3/12 over 14 days — both runners are outsiders on form, but Rothwell's activity level is worth noting in case market moves emerge pre-race.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Purse
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, which is a significant concern in a staying hurdle; genuine hold-up type whose best Good-ground form came over shorter (16f) and who has not threatened the frame in five runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Scarlet Purse has a tough ask from 151 lb and ranks 13th of 17 on our figures, though she has run over today's going before and the 25-day break gives connections every chance to present her fresh.

runners_data.name: Sekakarma
runners_data.note: Only 9 days since last run but has finished placed five times on Good including twice at 20f, showing this trip suits; Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant jockey booking and he can sit close enough to strike.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but rarely out of the frame, Sekakarma arrives here fresh on nine days' rest with experience over today's trip and conditions, though a 151 lb ask gives the handicapper the edge against a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: The Ducks Walk
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type remapped to midfield by field size; Good-ground form is solid (3/5 placings), handles distances up to 24f, and Conor's claim (5lbs) helps — but needs a trouble-free run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Ducks Walk at least returns quickly on 15 days' rest and has experience of today's trip and going, though carrying 150 lb and rated 11th of 17 by our assessors makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: Fading finisher flag makes this a concern in a 17-runner stamina test; true hold-up horse displaced forward on the map, and four runs at 22f+ without a win suggests he may just lack the finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Tantrum Boy has been winless in his last five starts, finishing fourth twice before that form tailed off badly, and our rating of 74 ranks him 16th of 17 here; weight of 146 lb adds further to the task, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Fenno's Soldier
runners_data.note: 1,345 days since last run — the longest absence in the field by a massive margin — and all four past runs came at shorter trips on Soft; even if the horse is fit, this is a wildly speculative profile.
runners_data.comment: Fenno's Soldier has been off the track for over three and a half years, making him deeply unexposed and open to significant improvement, though he arrives yet to win in his last four starts and faces a stern test carrying 145 lb on comeback.

runners_data.name: Little Boy Sivola
runners_data.note: Five-year-old wearing blinkers, flagged as a fader, and has yet to win in six starts; trainer Rothwell has 3/12 in 14 days but this horse pulled up last time and step back to Good ground is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a pull-up most recently, Little Boy Sivola faces an uphill task here, though he has run over today's going before and 35 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; carrying 145 lb looks a stiff ask at a mark of 77.

runners_data.name: Inches Away
runners_data.note: Fading finisher with a poor recent record (three 0s in five runs, three of those on Soft); the jump to Good ground and 20f trip is a question mark, and the hold-up style from deep is a further complication.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, Inches Away is hard to fancy at the weights despite having run over today's going before, with only a fourth last time out offering any crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cruisin Susan
runners_data.note: Has placed three times on Good at 20-24f, which is one of the more encouraging stamina profiles in the field; amateur Berry (7lbs) takes the weight down, and though she fades late, Wexford's galloping track may suit a staying challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Cruisin Susan does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and was third two starts back, though eighth last time out is harder to ignore, and 140 lb adds further pressure on a mark of 72.

runners_data.name: Duke Otto
runners_data.note: One of the higher-rated runners in the field (OR 98) without a jockey named — a flag to watch at declaration — and best form showed on Good with a win; hold-up profile suits if Chosen Princess sets a strong enough gallop.
runners_data.comment: Duke Otto has run over today's trip and going, our rating puts him among the leading contenders here, and 36 days between runs suggests connections have had time to plot a comeback — yet winless in his last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts in that sequence, the worry is whether he retains enough ability to deliver.

runners_data.name: Rumble Demosa
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old (only three runs recorded, all on Good), making it hard to assess, but all on this surface and stays 19f; trainer Griffin without a recent win but the unexposed angle gives him potential upside.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of 17 on our rating, Rumble Demosa does at least bring going experience to the table, though 158 lb is a sizeable burden and her recent string of unplaced efforts offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Warm In Gorey
runners_data.note: Seven place finishes on Good ground with trainer Rothwell in form (3/12 in 14 days); wears tongue tie and hood, stays well, and the consistent placing record at 17-20f makes him one of the more solid profiles to land from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Warm In Gorey has placed third three starts back and again four starts back, though back-to-back sixth-placed efforts since suggest he may be finding life harder; he has run over today's trip and going, but 164 lb is a stern ask.

races.paceDynamic: Chosen Princess is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press her early, she should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m4½f trip on Good ground. Sekakarma and Sharetheknowledge are the likeliest horses to sit prominently just behind her, giving the race a defined shape of one clear leader with a small cluster tracking. With the pace controlled and not pressured, horses racing in the prominent-to-midfield band will have the clearest sight of the winner, while the large group of hold-up types — including Warm In Gorey, Torque De Lune, Duke Otto and Cruisin Susan — will need to generate their own momentum from some way back. Several runners tagged as redistributed (Corkbeg, Scarlet Purse, Balinaboola Steel, The Ducks Walk and others) are true hold-up horses forced to map to midfield because the field simply cannot accommodate all rear-of-field runners in their natural position; of those, Sekabarma and Sharetheknowledge are best placed to actually secure a forward berth. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick from off the pace, or prominent trackers who can travel close to the controlled pace and strike from the home turn when Chosen Princess's lead is absorbed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chosen Princess Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Chosen Princess is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a gallop comfortable enough to sustain into the straight.
scenarios.body: She controls the tempo throughout, the field strings out on Good ground, and horses close enough to her early have a significant advantage when the race quickens from three out; hold-up types from deep positions face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out but those tracking two or three lengths off Chosen Princess travel sweetly and pounce from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Sekakarma and Sharetheknowledge, both sitting close to the pace with stamina at this trip, are ideally placed to challenge when Chosen Princess begins to tire late; the Good ground rewards their economical jumping style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Chosen Princess sets only a crawl early and the pace quickens sharply from halfway, compressing the race into a staying test that brings the closers into play.
scenarios.body: Warm In Gorey, with seven placed efforts on Good ground and strong course form, has the profile to reel in tiring rivals from off the pace; Torque De Lune's Good-ground form (5/7 runs) also gives him a chance if he can find a clear run in traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unfancied or lightly-raced runner produces an improved performance over this stamina-testing trip on a surface suiting it.
scenarios.body: Duke Otto's best form came on Good and he has winning form, while Rumble Demosa is lightly raced at five and unexposed at this trip; either could outrun their position if the race sets up with a sustainable gallop that rewards a late run.

watchPoints.text: Chosen Princess sets the entire tactical shape — if she is withdrawn or slow away, the race loses its only front-runner and the scenario probabilities shift entirely toward a muddling pace benefiting closers.
Duke Otto holds a significant OR advantage (98) over much of the field but has no jockey listed at time of analysis — confirm the rider, as a top booking here would make him a serious danger to all.

Fenno's Soldier (1,345 days off) and Balinaboola Steel (740 days off) both carry enormous fitness question marks; if either shows signs of distress early, jockeys may pull up and create interference in a packed 17-runner field.

With so many hold-up types compressed into midfield, watch for a traffic problem on the home turn — Torque De Lune and Warm In Gorey, both needing late runs, must find clear daylight from two out or their finishing efforts will be wasted.

Sekakarma ran just nine days ago; monitor paddock behaviour and jumping fluency early, as horses returning quickly can be either cherry-ripe or slightly flat — if he settles sweetly behind Chosen Princess, his race is on.

races.name: Traynors Of Wexford Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Forceonmyown
runners_data.note: OR=106 prominently raced Elliott runner with hurdle experience on good ground; best sim-going result was a third from nine starts on similar surface, no wins or places at listed level; 26 days off and 161lbs will test her in a deep 3m field.

runners_data.name: Something Fabulous
runners_data.note: Best-credentialled prominent racer here with a hurdle win and multiple places on good going, handled 22f last time out in a solid third; John McConnell has been in good form (4/27 over 14 days) and Alex Harvey provides a stable jockey link over a trip that should suit her stamina profile.

runners_data.name: Clody Diamond
runners_data.note: Prominent type who was second over 20f on good ground and placed at the trip; Paul Nolan's yard has a modest recent record (1/4) and 59 days off is the longest absence for any runner near the front of the market — jumping sharpness will need to be immediate.

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: S Curling's hold-up specialist has struggled on good ground throughout her career (0 wins, 0 places from 7 similar-going runs); her true style is wait-and-pounce from the rear, but with the prominent contingent dominating this field she is unlikely to secure the backmarker's berth she needs to produce her best.

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up mare who has placed five times over 19-21f on good going but never won; trained by her owner-handler, lightly supported by connections (0/1 over 14 days), and returning just 7 days after her last run — stamina is proven but a step up to 3m is new territory.

runners_data.name: Nancy Wheeler
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes; her last four runs show finishes of 8th, 15th, 11th and 14th on good ground and she has never converted a hold-up position into a placing — the combination of a suspect finish, amateur jockey, and this field size makes her deeply vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Pacy Macie
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two outings on good going over 24-25f, placing once; 7-day turnaround is quick but she has already shown an ability to handle the trip and surface, and a patient ride from Barry John Walsh could have her arriving late if the pace collapses the front rank.

runners_data.name: Queen Of The Gales
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and style unknown; her recent form string of P33-12 shows improving placings and a win, so she arrives on the upgrade — 96 days off and amateur jockey Collins are the main risks, but good ground should not be an issue based on limited profile.

runners_data.name: Star Cave
runners_data.note: Won nothing from nine runs but placed at 24f on good ground; style unknown and headgear flagged (ht), which suggests connections are experimenting — the long trip and lightly raced profile create considerable uncertainty over a stamina-testing 3m.

runners_data.name: Talladega
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here; has finished 4th and 5th from two good-ground starts over 22-24f and is mapped as prominent with a style-fit discount (0.93) — if she leads comfortably she controls the race shape entirely, but her own winning chance is tempered by a record of PP-P before those placings.

runners_data.name: Thornbury Queen
runners_data.note: Complete unknown: no form string, no last run date, no hist data, and style unknown — the headgear flag (h) suggests connections may be trying something new, and in a 13-runner maiden with this many rated runners she is the biggest question mark on the card.

runners_data.name: Where Eagles Fly
runners_data.note: Has run once on good ground, finishing 7th over 19f — that is her entire hurdles profile; 74 days off, amateur jockey, and a jump to 3m in a 13-runner field makes this a severe test; no meaningful pace data to project a likely shape.

runners_data.name: Burning Like Fire
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at four, flagged for fading in finishes; ran 14th on her only good-ground start over 18f and now faces a 3m trip — the step up in distance and the prominent style tag combining with a fade flag makes her late viability highly questionable, though Denis Hogan's yard has been active.

races.paceDynamic: Talladega is the confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 3m mares maiden hurdle on good ground at Wexford, and with only one genuine pace-setter in the field, the early gallop is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than searingly honest. Something Fabulous, Forceonmyown, Burning Like Fire, and Clody Diamond all carry prominent-racing profiles and will push forward, meaning there is a cluster fighting for position behind Talladega in the first mile, but none of them is a natural front-runner willing to go toe-to-toe from flag to flag. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate cleanly — Ellens Pride is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into midfield on the map, and is unlikely to secure a forward pitch in the actual race. With one uncontested pace-setter setting a steady tempo over 3m on a sound surface, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers with the stamina and jumping accuracy to track Talladega and pounce from the second-last, rather than true closers who need an end-to-end gallop to get home from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Talladega sets a measured gallop throughout and the prominent trackers travel comfortably into the final mile.
scenarios.body: Talladega dictates an unhurried tempo that compresses the field and keeps hold-up horses permanently disadvantaged, allowing the best prominent traveller to produce a clean challenge from the second-last flight and gallop to the line on the good surface. Something Fabulous, who has won and placed multiple times on good ground at this sort of trip, and Forceonmyown, racing out of Gordon Elliott's yard with experience over fences, are ideally placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Talladega's early dominance sets a genuine searching gallop that exposes stamina limitations in the prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected early pace over this demanding 3m trip would string the field out and bring the hold-up horses — those who can genuinely be produced late — into play in the closing stages. Pacy Macie, who has form over 24-25f on good going, and Lakewood Rose, who has shown consistency over 19-21f, could emerge from midfield if prominent rivals stop on the long run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Market Mover Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced or unexposed runners — Queen Of The Gales or Thornbury Queen — improves sharply on their profile and travels into contention.
scenarios.body: With several unexposed runners carrying OR=120 and unknown style tags, a maiden hurdle over 3m on good ground is exactly the context where an unraced-type can bloom; Queen Of The Gales has finished 1-2-3 in her last two starts and Thornbury Queen is a complete unknown. A smooth jumping display and a prominent position could allow either to hit the line before the stable, experienced types have time to respond.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the prominent runners burn themselves out fighting for position in the first half of the race.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a fast pace that fractures the field and allows the true hold-up horses to sweep past tired rivals on the run to the last — but Ellens Pride, the most natural closer here, has been redistributed and is unlikely to settle at the rear in a race with this many prominent types. Lakewood Rose and Nancy Wheeler, despite poor recent form, remain the most plausible beneficiaries if the pace genuinely collapses the front rank, though Nancy Wheeler's finish-fading flag is a major concern.

watchPoints.text: Talladega controls the entire pace equation — if she jumps poorly early or is challenged for the lead by Something Fabulous or Forceonmyown, the settled gallop fractures and all scenario probabilities shift significantly toward stamina-testing territory.

Something Fabulous arrives on just a 12-day turnaround with the best good-ground profile in the field; watch whether Alex Harvey positions her directly on Talladega's heels from the off, as that tracking move is the simplest path to a winning chance.

Queen Of The Gales is 96 days off the track with an unknown style and an improving form string — if she jumps well and travels into the race, her lightly raced profile could be significantly underestimated by the market.

Ellens Pride's redistribution is a genuine race-shape signal — if she is unable to settle at the rear and gets dragged into mid-division scrimmaging, the closers' scenario loses its most credible catalyst and the prominent runners' advantage increases further.

With four runners carrying OR=120 and flagged as style=U (unknown), Thornbury Queen in particular is a total wildcard; any market move on her before the off should be noted, as connections may have information that the public form book cannot show.

races.name: Brendan Cullimore Electrical Rated Novice Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Le Coq Hardi
runners_data.note: The Henry De Bromhead-trained seven-year-old arrives on 29 days' rest with strong Good-ground form (13 from 15 in similar conditions) and a clear front-running mandate here; OR 133 gives him the class edge, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution that the prominent tag slightly undersells how much he wants to lead.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has won twice at 20f on Good ground and Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is attractive on a 163lb weight; naturally prominent, he is the most likely horse to track Le Coq Hardi closely if he cannot take the lead himself, and his Good-ground record (9 from 13) underpins his chances.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Andrew McNamara, Warriors Wood has shown he can win from off the pace (three wins from 11 on Good ground) and his form at 20-23f is solid; he needs a stronger pace than Le Coq Hardi is likely to set, which is the key tactical risk in this shape.

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly's eight-year-old mare arrives 42 days fresh and is a natural prominent racer — she has won twice at 16-17f on Good — but the redistribution reflects that she cannot hold that position in this shape; her best form has come at shorter distances, and stepping to 2m3½f over fences on a compressed schedule adds modest stamping concerns.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Timothy Doyle's seven-year-old has a modest recent form string (772U74) and the amateur rider Mr D Doyle carries 7lbs of claim at 152lbs; Good ground is not a concern (12 from 15), but the horse lacks the class or tactical speed to threaten unless chaos unfolds at the front.

races.paceDynamic: Le Coq Hardi is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressurise him, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m3½f trip on Good ground at Wexford. Ma Jacks Hill and Femme Magnifique are both natural prominent types, but with Le Coq Hardi already owning that role, at least one of them will be shuffled back from their preferred position — the field contains more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, and Le Coq Hardi is most likely to secure the lead, with Ma Jacks Hill the next-best placed to sit just off it. The resulting dynamic is a measured, unhurried tempo that will keep the pace honest rather than searching, giving a strong galloper the chance to dominate from the front without ever being headed. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can travel comfortably in the first two and produce a sustained jump-by-jump grind rather than a late burst — true hold-up horses like Warriors Wood and Beauforts Storm will need more generous pace to set up their finishes than this race is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Le Coq Hardi Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Le Coq Hardi bowls along at a controlled tempo, holds a clear lead and jumps fluently throughout.
scenarios.body: O'Keeffe engineers a frictionless front-running display, the moderate pace suiting Le Coq Hardi's stamina and class advantage at OR 133; rivals are never able to reel him in from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Ma Jacks Hill or Femme Magnifique manages to push up and harry Le Coq Hardi, creating a contested prominent duel.
scenarios.body: A marginally more pressured gallop tests Le Coq Hardi's jumping accuracy and opens the door for the best traveller in behind; a horse who can sit a close second and pounce at the last benefits most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or leaders blunder late, allowing a prominent closer to scythe through on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Warriors Wood, with a strong record on Good ground and a genuine hold-up profile, is the only true closer here with the form credentials to capitalise on a late meltdown at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition and Errors
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors eliminate or fatally check the fancied horses, turning the race into a staying-power contest.
scenarios.body: Beauforts Storm, a durable type who has stayed on in defeat before, could inherit a place; the amateur rider Mr D Doyle on board means this scenario is only viable through mishap rather than merit.

watchPoints.text: Warriors Wood — his chances hinge entirely on whether Le Coq Hardi sets enough of a gallop to stretch the field; if the pace is truly pedestrian, Daniel King will have nowhere to aim and his hold-up style becomes a liability.

Femme Magnifique — watch for a tardy start or a scramble for position in the early stages; as a true prominent type squeezed to midfield on the map, any traffic trouble in the first mile could cost Danny Gilligan the race before it has begun.

Le Coq Hardi — for all the tactical advantages, Darragh O'Keeffe must ensure the jumping is fluent; a blunder at any of the steeplechase fences at a controlled pace could gift rivals an unearned momentum swing.

Ma Jacks Hill — Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is worth monitoring at the weights; if he can slot in second and travel comfortably, the Elliott runner could be better placed than the market might suggest in a small-field novice chase.

Beauforts Storm — the amateur rider angle and modest OR 112 make this horse one to watch only if the race descends into attrition; at 37 days since last run with no meaningful recent form boost, he is primarily a race-shape marker rather than a genuine threat.

races.name: Dan & Breda Byrne Memorial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Farrokh
runners_data.note: Won last time at 16f on good, Sean Flanagan in the plate for Barry Connell whose yard is 0/1 in the 14-day window — prominent style suits tracking the front pair here, and his sim-going record of 15/15 on good underlines he handles conditions; 37-day break is no concern given his recent winning comeback.|
runners_data.comment: Farrokh won last time out and has run over today's trip and conditions before, lending him some solid claims; the 37-day gap and a hefty 166 lb to carry are the chief questions to resolve.

runners_data.name: Sammy Smart
runners_data.note: Aged 10 and his form string shows pulls-up and unseats recently, with his last win coming at 22f on good — Darragh O'Keeffe can hold him up but this horse has been inconsistent and his trainer has sent out 0/3 in the 14-day window, making him hard to trust at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sammy Smart at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and at 166 lb he faces a stiff ask — yet our rating just about edges him ahead of his rivals, making him the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 23f on good last time for a trainer in form (1/4 T14), but he carries an amateur rider (Mr B T Stone, 7lb claim) which raises questions about whether he can fully exploit the lead against Kasper Hauser — sim-going record of 7/8 on good is encouraging but the amateur is a real variable.|
runners_data.comment: Catalani arrives in cracking form, winning last time out and placing in two of the three starts before that, and his experience on today's going is a further asset; the weight burden of 165 lb is the one factor worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 114, has won his last two starts including over 22f on good, and races off a headgear flag (h) — Calum Hogan's 5lb claim is an asset on weight but the horse is only 4 years old and a confirmed front-runner who will have to share the lead with Catalani rather than enjoy it; trainer has sent out 0/9 in the 14-day window which is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Kasper Hauser arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and shaped with promise when third three starts back, making him a potent force here; carrying 163 lb off a mark of 114 is the chief concern against him.

runners_data.name: Luimneach
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won last time over 20f on good and placed on soft, with Charlie O'Dwyer (3lb claim) for Conor O'Dwyer — headgear tags h and t suggest a horse that needs restraining, and the 35-day gap since his win is manageable; genuinely suited by a fast-run race where he can finish past beaten rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Luimneach arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making him a clear threat on our third-best rating; the main concern is that two of his last five starts brought a pull-up and a fifth, highlighting some inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Giant Haystacks
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good earlier in the season for Ross O'Sullivan, whose yard has sent out 0/20 in the last 14 days — prominent style and a solid sim-going record make him a natural to sit just off the pace, but trainer form at the course is too cold to ignore; headgear (t) suggests he needs restraining.|
runners_data.comment: Showed he can win at this level when scoring two starts back, but has disappointed since and returns after 31 days with a trainer who has drawn a blank in 20 attempts over the past fortnight; 161 lb is no help either.

runners_data.name: The Burrow
runners_data.note: 126 days off the track is a major flag, and his form string of 9-6-5-9-5 on good at similar trips suggests he is a consistent maiden at this level — the hold-up style means he would need a truly run race to peel off the back and his 0W0P record in similar going conditions makes this a tough assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked second-bottom of our figures here, The Burrow faces a stiff task carrying 159 lb on a lengthy 126-day absence, though he does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Has won and placed multiple times at 16f on good ground with Philip Enright (a strong jockey booking) — the headgear (p) is a positive for a 10-year-old, and his recent form of 125 shows genuine competitiveness; the step up to 2m3½f from his preferred 16f trips is the key query, though his latest win came at 17f.|
runners_data.comment: Chosen Shant won three starts back and was second two starts back, but dropped to fifth last time out and carries a hefty 153 lb here; she has run over today's trip and going, and her profile suggests she's capable but this weight makes life harder.

runners_data.name: Auntie Lacey
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan sends her out 59 days since her last run with headgear (t and p), and her sim-going record of 8/8 on good shows she handles conditions well — a hold-up type who has never won but placed once in similar going, she is best watched for an improved run if freshness works in her favour.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Auntie Lacey faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, but a 59-day absence and a burden of 151 lb make it hard to fancy her fortunes improving.

runners_data.name: Stily
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on good ground (14/15 sim-going) with five placed efforts but no wins — this horse's natural instinct is to race prominently but with four other horses wanting that position the field crowds him back, meaning he is likely to race out of role in midfield; his best efforts have come when racing handily, so the congested shape is a genuine negative.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Stily is hard to fancy here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the 25-day break at least suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Kasper Hauser and Catalani are the two confirmed front-runners and will dispute the lead from the off over 2m3½f on good ground at Wexford, creating an honest, competitive gallop that is unlikely to relent. Farrokh, Sammy Smart, Giant Haystacks, and Chosen Shant all want prominent positions, meaning the first three fences will see significant jostling and potential traffic incidents, particularly rounding the bend 2-3 out. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Kasper Hauser (OR 114, two wins from last three) and Catalani (recent winner, yard in form) are likeliest to actually hold the lead, with Farrokh and Giant Haystacks best placed to sit just off them, while Stily, a natural prominent racer, is pushed back into a midfield role against its instincts. A genuinely contested pace across the full trip on good ground favours horses with proven stamina who can travel mid-division and finish, giving hold-up types like Luimneach and the prominent-but-patient Chosen Shant a realistic chance of picking up the pieces from those burned in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Kasper Hauser and Catalani burn each other up in a genuine duel and the prominent cluster gets crowded out 2-3 from home.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop set by the two front-runners depletes those who chased them into the race, leaving the race to come apart in the straight for runners who have been held up or have travelled within themselves mid-race. Luimneach, a confirmed hold-up type returning to good ground with two recent top-two finishes, and Chosen Shant, who has won and placed repeatedly at this sort of trip on good, are both ideally suited to finish past the spent leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates Fully
scenarios.trigger: If Kasper Hauser (OR 114, top-rated, claiming rider Calum Hogan 5lb) dictates at a controlled tempo and gets the rail throughout without being pushed into overdrive.
scenarios.body: Kasper Hauser has won his last two starts, is top-rated in the field, and jumps well enough to find a rhythm that saps his rivals without burning himself — if Catalani is unable to match him early and drops away, Kasper Hauser dictates the fractions and simply runs the race on his terms. This is the shape most dangerous for hold-up horses who need pace to exploit, and a clean round of jumping from a 4-year-old who is improving rapidly makes this a genuine threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves honest but not excessive and the race resolves in favour of those who tracked the leaders without overcommitting early.
scenarios.body: Farrokh, who won last time on similar good ground at 16f and is ridden by Sean Flanagan, or Giant Haystacks, a course-proven winner on good ground with solid recent form, sit close enough to pounce if the leaders slow or make a jumping error at the last. This shape rewards those who were prominent enough to control the race but never led, and both horses have the fitness and going profile to see it out at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest causes fallers or departures at fences and the race degenerates into a small-field scramble in the final mile.
scenarios.body: With 10 runners, two genuine front-runners and a congested prominent group, interference or jumping errors mid-race could fragment the field unpredictably, leaving a well-handicapped or lower-rated runner to creep through late. Chosen Shant (recent win and two places, Phillip Enright aboard) and Auntie Lacey (Paul Nolan stable, returning fresh) are the types to benefit from attrition in a messy race if chaos strips the field of its principals.

watchPoints.text: Catalani and Kasper Hauser — both confirmed front-runners likely to lock horns from the first fence, and whichever one is pressured into an unsustainable gallop early becomes a significant faller/early exit risk at the open ditches.

Stily — racing against its natural prominent instinct and mapped to midfield by field congestion, there is a meaningful risk of being squeezed wide or losing position entirely on the first bend, making it vulnerable to traffic interference.

The Burrow — 126 days off the course with a form string that has not included a top-six finish since 2023; if this horse jumps sluggishly on return, it becomes an obstacle for the prominent group rounding the bend 2-3 out.

Chosen Shant — Phillip Enright takes over for the first time and the switch to 2m3½f is unproven, so watch how he travels at halfway; if he is still going well entering the back straight final time the longer trip may be within him.

Luimneach — rider Charlie O'Dwyer will deliberately hold this horse up off a genuine pace, but Wexford's tight track means leaving ground at the rear in a 10-runner chase is a real risk if the field fans wide on the final turn.

runners_data.name: North Of Nashville
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on good ground 37 days ago for Colin Bowe, who has a lean T14 record of 0/2; a hold-up operator whose best sim-going return shows 2 wins and 2 places from 15 runs, and the step back up in trip from recent outings looks a positive.|

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer who raced only 14 days ago and has placed twice from eight runs on good ground; John Shinnick takes the ride and the horse shapes as a reliable tracker who will try to be competitive from the front without ever threatening to dominate.|
runners_data.comment: Thewaybackhome has run over today's trip and going, and that second two starts back shows he can get competitive, but he remains winless in his last five and a career-high 158 lb is no small ask for a gelding ranked seventh of sixteen.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old with an outstanding good-ground record — 15 from 15 runs on similar going including three wins and seven placed efforts — and trainer John G Carr is in form at 2/5 over 14 days; the seven-day turnaround with tongue-tie applied is the only note of caution over this extended trip.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 16 on our figures and 8 lb below his official mark in our assessment, Fr Gilligansvoyge is hard to fancy despite a lively recent record that includes three wins in his last six starts; the weight of 157 lb adds further concern.

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Prominent-style seven-year-old whose recent form string shows a pull-up and a fifth as his last two completions, and the amateur rider (7lb claim) adds risk; the tongue-tie is retained but sim-going figures of 13 places from 15 runs suggest he hangs around competitively without winning.|
runners_data.comment: Je Suis arrives on the back of a pulled-up effort eight days ago, but her experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 94 that ranks her second in this field, marks her out as a leading contender; the risk is that she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Gift
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse carrying 156lbs for John M Burke (T14 0/2) whose recent form includes a fall and a pulled-up, and his best sim-going record shows just one placed effort from 11 runs on good; trip and current form do not inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Charlie's Gift has a troubled recent profile — falling and pulling up in consecutive starts before an eighth last time out — and yet to win in his last five, he faces a stiff task off 156 lb, though experience on today's going and a rating of 91 offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent recent form profile — second, first, fourth, fifth, second across his last five runs on good ground — and Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claim) adds value; the eight-day turnaround is noted but the blinkers and consistent placing record make him a key tracking danger.|
runners_data.comment: Cullenwaine ran second last time out and was a winner two starts back, so he arrives in form, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the weight of 155 lb and a rating of 84 in a 16-runner field are limiting factors.

runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old hold-up horse whose recent form shows an eighth and a ninth, and sim-going record of 3 wins and 4 places from 15 runs tells a better story than current form; age and recent performances make it hard to be enthused despite the handicap mark of OR 84.|
runners_data.comment: Stormy Master showed when third three starts back that he retains ability, and with experience over today's trip and going, plus 24 days of freshness, the gelding is weighted to outrun his official mark of 84 despite being winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; trainer David Kenneth Budds has a sharp T14 strike of 2/3, Darragh O'Keeffe steers, and the horse has been consistently placed at shorter trips — the step up to 3m1f is a question mark but the uncontested lead is a significant tactical gift.|
runners_data.comment: Oogum Boogum showed his best a winner and runner-up in his last six starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but back-to-back sevenths and eighths weigh against him despite a rating of 91 and a reasonable 24-day break.

runners_data.name: True Harmony
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old tagged as fading in the finish, which is a meaningful concern over 3m1f; sim-going record of only 4 from 8 on similar going and one place from four completed runs suggests modest ability, and Philip Donovan's trainer has no runs in the 14-day window.|
runners_data.comment: True Harmony is winless in his last five starts, though a second three starts back shows he can get competitive, and he has run over today's trip and going; two consecutive sixth-place finishes weigh against him under 151 lb from a ranking of eleventh in the field.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose true racing style places him at the rear of the field; his sim-going record is a standout 15 from 15 on good ground with a win and four places, but racing effectively out of role in a crowded midfield group — the STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 means his tactical disadvantage should weigh against him.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with a fall among his recent outings, U Asking Me carries 147 lb and arrives on a quick 14-day turnaround; he has run over today's trip and going before, but his patchy profile makes him a tough one to trust.

runners_data.name: Mini Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent nine-year-old whose best recent runs include a win over 24f on good ground and a second over the same trip; Alex Harvey rides for M M Lynch (T14 1/1) and the sim-going record of 5 from 11 with two placed efforts is modest but his tracking profile suits the likely race shape better than many below him in the market.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and her recent form has been patchy, with three unplaced or minor finishes in her last four starts before a win four starts back; has run over today's trip and going, but it is hard to make a case for her at these weights.

runners_data.name: Urbs Intacta Manet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old five-year-old whose natural inclination is to race from the rear, pushed into a midfield position on the map by the density of hold-up types in this field; fading in the finish is flagged, sim-going numbers are weak at 3 from 7 with zero wins or places, and Daniel King's mount looks vulnerable at this demanding trip.|

runners_data.name: Three County Star
runners_data.note: Another true hold-up five-year-old that the race shape has displaced into midfield; fades-in-finish flag is present, the form string shows a pulled-up and three single-digit finishes, and the good-ground record of 9 from 13 with zero wins tells you the ability level clearly — Calum Hogan (5lb claim) rides for trainer Brian Mortell.|
runners_data.comment: Three County Star arrives in good order on 18 days' rest, has experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 93 marks him out as a serious threat in this field — but a run of modest finishes in recent starts, including a pull-up, is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Barely Made It
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose hold-up style leaves him naturally disadvantaged in a race already crowded at the rear; Colin Bowe's yard (T14 0/2) also runs North Of Nashville, and while a third-place effort 37 days ago over 24f on good is encouraging, the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 applies and the trip is longer than his best.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Barely Made It faces a stiff ask here, though she does return on experience over today's trip and going, and a third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Tennesse Boy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose last three starts are all pulled-ups, and a fades-in-finish flag compounds the concern; Phillip Enright rides for Robert Tyner (no T14 runs) and with sim-going showing 9 from 12 runs the underlying aptitude for good ground exists, but current form makes it very difficult to trust over 3m1f.|
runners_data.comment: Tennesse Boy has pulled up in three of his last five starts and is winless in that sequence, with only a second two runs further back offering any encouragement; ranked last on our figures and carrying 141 lb, he faces a stiff task here.

races.paceDynamic: Oogum Boogum is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field over 3m1f on good ground at Wexford, and with no genuine rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. The pace will be honest rather than frenetic — a lone leader at this trip on good ground sets a rhythm that is unlikely to collapse but equally unlikely to produce a scorching early tempo that stretches the field. Prominent racers sitting just off Oogum Boogum — particularly Fr Gilligansvoyge, Cullenwaine and Thewaybackhome — will travel comfortably in the slipstream and be best positioned to pounce when the race quickens from the third-last. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear; U Asking Me, Urbs Intacta Manet, Three County Star, Barely Made It and Tennesse Boy are all true hold-up horses redistributed to the midfield map position because the rear of the field is oversubscribed, and the most likely beneficiaries of the actual race shape are the genuine prominent runners who can track the leader through the race without expending energy fighting for position. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent, front-tracking profiles who can sit within a length or two of Oogum Boogum's controlled pace and produce their effort from the second-last fence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Oogum Boogum sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent racers track him comfortably before asserting from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Oogum Boogum's lack of competition for the lead means Fr Gilligansvoyge, Cullenwaine and Thewaybackhome can travel sweetly in behind without burning energy, and the one who produces the sharpest jump at the second-last fence takes control. Fr Gilligansvoyge's excellent good-ground form (three wins, seven placed from 15 runs on similar going) and in-form trainer give this profile the strongest case.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Oogum Boogum, with T14 form of 2/3 and a clear lead, gradually extends his advantage and the prominent horses expend energy trying to close.
scenarios.body: At 3m1f on good ground with no pressure, Oogum Boogum could find his own rhythm and, if the chasing pack misjudge the pace or meet a fence wrong, his lead could become unassailable late. Darragh O'Keeffe's tactical awareness and the horse's recent consistency (placed three times in five) make this a credible threat even from OR 82.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfielders Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If Oogum Boogum sets a slow early tempo that brings the true midfielders into contention and a staying battle develops from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A muddling pace over this marathon trip can compress the field and allow horses like North Of Nashville, Hit The Frame or Mini Getaway — who prefer to come from off the pace — to arrive with a late run when tiring rivals fade. North Of Nashville's sole win in this form string came over 26f on good ground, and Hit The Frame won over 25f on good ground, giving both a staying profile that could suit a falsely-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Fallers Aid Tail-Enders
scenarios.trigger: If the race is disrupted by falls or the pace accelerates sharply mid-race, leaving genuine hold-up types to arrive late on a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: In a 16-runner steeplechase over 3m1f, attrition is always possible, and if enough prominent horses tire or exit, redistributed hold-up types such as U Asking Me or Barely Made It could find daylight they would never otherwise see. Their style-fit discounts are real — they are unlikely to be in their preferred position — but carnage ahead can override tactical disadvantage over this trip.

watchPoints.text: Fr Gilligansvoyge's seven-day turnaround is tight for a 13-year-old going up in trip to 3m1f — monitor market moves and any official comments about the horse's wellbeing before the off, as fatigue late could undermine an otherwise strong profile.

Oogum Boogum's uncontested lead over 3m1f is the defining tactical variable — if he gets away unchallenged and sets a deceptively slow early gallop, prominent horses like Thewaybackhome or Cullenwaine could be caught flat-footed when the tempo suddenly lifts at the third-last.

Hit The Frame's 104-day layoff demands scrutiny — a hold-up horse returning from nearly three and a half months off over a stamina trip at Wexford is vulnerable to ring-rustiness, and Jordan Canavan's 7lb claim does not fully compensate for that fitness question.

With five runners tagged as redistributed hold-up types forced into midfield, watch for a scrimmage in the first half-mile as horses fight for position — any interference or early jumping errors in a bunched midfield group could affect several runners simultaneously.

Cullenwaine and Thewaybackhome both raced eight and fourteen days ago respectively, giving them racecourse sharpness that cold rivals cannot match — their recent appearances over similar going are a practical advantage in a field where several horses are returning from meaningful breaks.
